questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.

questions.questionText: Which statement about factors of production is correct?

options.A: All economic output requires the use of four factors of production.
options.B: Capital may take the form of shares in a manufacturing company.
options.C: Enterprise can only be found in owner-run organisations.
options.D: Land includes both renewable and non-renewable resources.

questions.questionText: A farmer can produce both wheat and barley at constant costs of production. The opportunity cost of a kilo of wheat is 1.5 kilos of barley. The price of a kilo of wheat is twice that of barley. What should the farmer do to maximise revenue?

options.A: Concentrate on barley production.
options.B: Concentrate on wheat production.
options.C: Produce wheat and barley in the ratio 2:1.
options.D: Produce wheat and barley in the ratio 3:2.

The price elasticity of demand for a product is inelastic. How will a decrease in supply affect producer revenue and consumer surplus? producer revenue consumer surplus

options.A: fall fall
options.B: fall rise
options.C: rise fall
options.D: rise rise

options.A: As price rises, the price elasticity of supply of S will increase.
options.B: At any price, the price elasticity of supply of S will be less than that of S .

questions.questionText: Demand for shoes increases which pushes up their price. Firm Y increases its supply more quickly than firm Z. What would explain this difference in the speed of their responses?

options.A: Firm Y has limited stocks of unsold shoes whereas firm Z has plentiful stocks of unsold shoes.
options.B: Firm Y has spare capacity in its factories whereas firm Z’s factories are working at full capacity.
options.C: Firm Y’s shoes are handmade whereas firm Z’s shoes are made by machine.
options.D: Firm Y’s shoes need raw materials which are in short supply whereas firm Z’s shoes need raw materials which are in plentiful supply.

questions.questionText: In a free market in disequilibrium, which combination of price and quantity will lead to a fall in price and a contraction in output to reach equilibrium? S P P price P D O Q Q Q
In which set of circumstances will prices not be able to perform their function as an allocative mechanism, but may still have a role as a rationing device?

options.A: The government sets maximum prices for all goods above their market clearing price.
options.B: The government sets minimum wages for all workers below the market rates of pay.
options.C: The quantities of all goods available to consumers are in fixed supply.
options.D: The total income consumers have available to spend is fixed.

Which statement about the provision of goods is correct?

options.A: Governments and private producers supply merit goods.
options.B: Governments and private producers supply public goods.
options.C: Governments are unable to supply private goods.
options.D: Governments subsidise the production of demerit goods.

questions.questionText: A country exports olives. The government is involved in their production because it wishes to ensure that private producers of olives have the confidence to plan investment despite changes in the harvest of olives. Which economic term would describe this situation?

options.A: a command economy
options.B: a constant income elasticity
options.C: an export quota
options.D: a price stabilisation policy

options.A: a fall in the price of rice
options.B: an advertising campaign for bread
options.C: an increased wheat harvest
options.D: an increase in subsidies to wheat farmers

questions.questionText: Country X exports agricultural commodities to country Y and country Y exports industrial goods to country X. Given that the pattern of trade between X and Y can be explained by the theory of comparative advantage, what can be concluded from this?

options.A: Both countries derive an equal benefit from engaging in trade.
options.B: Country X has more fertile agricultural land than country Y.
options.C: Neither country has an absolute advantage in the production of both sets of goods.
options.D: The opportunity cost of producing agricultural commodities is greater in Y than in X.

questions.questionText: What is not usually a motive for a country to use protection in international trade?

options.A: to increase global economic welfare
options.B: to prevent the dumping of products by another country
options.C: to prevent unemployment within the country
options.D: to shelter an infant industry within the country

questions.questionText: A government decides to increase a quota on an imported good. What is likely to happen?

options.A: The demand for the good will fall.
options.B: The good will become more expensive.
options.C: The government’s revenue will decline.
options.D: There will be more of the good imported.

questions.questionText: A Japanese car manufacturer sets up a factory to produce car parts in Malaysia. How is this likely to affect Malaysia’s trade balance and its income balance in the current account of the balance of payments? trade balance income balance

options.A: improve improve
options.B: improve worsen
options.C: worsen improve
options.D: worsen worsen

questions.questionText: The weighting given to food in the construction of the United Kingdom’s Retail Price Index fell from 16.7% in 1987 to 11.8% in 2011. What would help to explain this?

options.A: The average price of food decreased by 4.9% points between 1987 and 2011.
options.B: The demand for food is price inelastic.
options.C: The income elasticity of the demand for food is less than one.
options.D: There was an increase in the relative price of food over the period.

This results in an increase in consumer expenditure which shifts the aggregate demand curve to the right, as shown. LRAS SRAS general price P level P AD AD O Y Y real GDP What could cause the economy’s output to return to Y?

options.A: a decrease in indirect taxes
options.B: a decrease in tariffs on imports
options.C: an increase in investment
options.D: an increase in wage rates

questions.questionText: Which statement about inflation is correct?

options.A: Cost-push inflation is likely to occur when the government increases its expenditure.
options.B: Demand-pull inflation is likely to occur when the country’s exchange rate appreciates.
options.C: The Quantity Theory of Money predicts that changes in money supply can cause inflation.
options.D: When inflation is unanticipated real values remain unchanged.

questions.questionText: A country experienced an annual inflation rate of 4% for three successive years. Which statement is correct for the three-year period?

options.A: The price level rose by 12%.
options.B: The price level rose by more than 12%.
options.C: The real value of money rose by 12%.
options.D: The real value of money rose by more than 12%.

questions.questionText: Why might an increase in a current account surplus cause inflation?

options.A: It will decrease aggregate supply.
options.B: It will decrease the money supply.
options.C: It will increase aggregate demand.
options.D: It will increase the exchange rate.

questions.questionText: Demand for imports is often price inelastic in the short term. Over time, demand tends to become more price elastic. What does this help to explain?

options.A: why a fall in the exchange rate causes a deficit on the current account of the balance of payments to increase before decreasing
options.B: why a fall in the exchange rate causes inflation to rise before falling
options.C: why a rise in the exchange rate causes a surplus on the current account of the balance of payments to decrease before increasing
options.D: why a rise in the exchange rate causes the terms of trade to worsen before improving
